title: UI Laws for Chips, Hover, Bands, Drag, Toggles, Icons and Lines
description: UI inconsistencies seen on the architecture and technology course site but affecting the UI in general. (1) All chips are conceptually one layer higher than the element they sit on: they need a different, tinted glass background through which the content below stays visible; e.g. on the cards overview the chips currently have the same background as the card. (2) The hover effect currently adds an additional border around an element. This must never happen: emphasis only ever happens on existing borders and on the foreground (text, icon) of a UI element.
summary: Ten UI laws fixed in the shared UI module and the course site: chips carry a foreground-veil glass tint; hover recolours existing lines and never adds one; pages, grids and dialogs tile edge to edge; navbar and footer are panel-level glass bands the content scrolls beneath; a dragged task element is detached with all drop places shown; clip posters fill the card under the chips; no rounded corner or shadow, native tick boxes drawn square; the challenge is a chip-titled card of toggle cells and switches are toggle cells; every shared course control requires an icon; a line shared with a band is painted by the band. Verified: TypeScript border law and compositor tests pass (9, 16, 13, 45, 11), each law checked in the browser on the course site. Not verified: all Rust changes (outline law, Theme::chip_glass, wgpu chip sites) are uncompiled, the graph test run failed twice on infrastructure (stale dependency receipt, then dependencies image out of space); no TypeScript type check; DOM component suites not run; several course screens not opened. See summary.md in the ticket folder.
